content:
# Sampling-variability app, linear-model VERSION B (one predictor: a test, or gender)
#
# Compares ONE observed (simulated) dataset's slope b and R^2 with two representations of
# sampling variability: four more datasets from the same population, and two piles of
# 100 simulated studies (H0 true / HA true). All logic lives in
# ../nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b.R; this file is only the interface.
#
# Version B = the Version C app (nhst-sampling-variability-lm-app/) without Phase C: no age,
# no "Also adjust for" boxes, no added-variable plots. See
# nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b-walkthrough.qmd.
#
# Run from the project root with:
#   shiny::runApp("nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b-app")
#
# Requires: shiny, bslib, ggplot2, ggdist, MASS.

library(shiny)
library(bslib)
library(ggplot2)

# Helper scripts: looked for next to this file first (for a deployed bundle), then in the
# project root (the folder above this one).
src <- function(f) source(if (file.exists(f)) f else file.path("..", f))
src("psych-battery-dgp.R")
src("nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R")
src("nhst-sampling-variability.R")
src("nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b.R")

random_seed <- function() sample.int(10000, 1)

# Fewer value labels under the slider: the default labelling crowds the largest values at
# the right-hand end. data-grid-num is the ionRangeSlider option for the number of grid
# intervals (4 intervals = 5 labels: -max, -max/2, 0, max/2, max). shiny sets its own value
# first, so that one is removed (adding would just append a second value to the attribute).
few_ticks <- function(slider, n = 4) {
  htmltools::tagQuery(slider)$find("input.js-range-slider")$
    removeAttrs("data-grid-num")$addAttrs(`data-grid-num` = n)$allTags()
}

x_default <- "ART3"
y_default <- "StuVoc1"
limit_default <- lm_slope_limit(x_default, y_default)

# Slider label for the current predictor / units.
slider_label <- function(x, units) {
  if (units == "std") return("Population standardised beta (= r)")
  if (lm_is_binary(x)) "Population mean difference b (M - F, points)" else "Population slope b (raw units)"
}

# Choices offered for the outcome: with a test as predictor the outcome is the other test (one
# choice, so the box shows it but cannot change it); with gender either test can be the outcome.
y_choices <- function(x) if (lm_is_binary(x)) lm_var_choices else lm_var_choices[lm_var_choices == lm_other_var(x)]

# The outcome: the other test, unless the predictor is gender (then the Outcome selector decides).
outcome_of <- function(x, y_input) if (lm_is_binary(x)) y_input else lm_other_var(x)

# Largest slider value in standardised units, rounded down to the slider's step.
std_slider_limit <- function() floor(sv_r_limits[2] / 0.05 + 1e-9) * 0.05


# ---- User interface ------------------------------------------------------------------

ui <- page_fillable(
  title = "Sampling variability: the slope and R-squared of a linear model",
  theme = bs_theme(version = 5),
  padding = 12,
  gap = 12,

  # Compact control card: tighter spacing between inputs and around the card's contents
  tags$head(tags$style(HTML("
    .ctl .card-body { padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; gap: 0; }
    .ctl .shiny-input-container { margin-bottom: 0.2rem; }
    .ctl .form-label, .ctl .control-label { margin-bottom: 0.1rem; }
    .ctl .form-check { margin-bottom: 0; min-height: 1.2rem; }
    .ctl .irs { margin-top: 0.1rem; }
  "))),

  card(
    fill = FALSE,
    class = "py-0 ctl",
    layout_columns(
      col_widths = c(2, 3, 3, 2, 2),
      selectizeInput("n", "N per study", choices = sv_n_choices, selected = 30,
                     width = "100%", options = list(dropdownParent = "body")),
      selectInput("x_var", "Predictor (X)", choices = lm_x_choices, selected = x_default,
                  width = "100%"),
      selectInput("y_var", "Outcome (Y)", choices = y_choices(x_default), selected = y_default,
                  width = "100%"),
      numericInput("seed", "Seed", value = random_seed(), min = 1, max = 10000, step = 1,
                   width = "100%"),
      div(
        class = "d-flex flex-column justify-content-center h-100 gap-1",
        actionButton("new_samples", "Draw new samples", class = "btn-primary btn-sm w-100"),
        actionButton("new_piles", "Redraw the piles", class = "btn-outline-secondary btn-sm w-100"),
        checkboxInput("zoom", "Zoom to piles", value = FALSE, width = "100%")
      )
    ),
    layout_columns(
      class = "mt-3",
      col_widths = c(8, 4),
      # Slider package: label and units buttons on one line, the slider below
      div(
        div(class = "d-flex justify-content-between align-items-baseline gap-3",
            tags$label(class = "control-label fw-bold", `for` = "beta", textOutput("slider_title", inline = TRUE)),
            radioButtons("units", NULL, choices = c("Raw units" = "raw", "Standardised" = "std"),
                         selected = "raw", inline = TRUE)),
        few_ticks(sliderInput("beta", NULL, min = -limit_default, max = limit_default,
                              value = 0.2, step = 0.01, width = "100%"))
      ),
      # Under the seed box: model and statistic
      div(
        div(class = "small text-muted mb-1", uiOutput("model_note")),
        radioButtons("stat", NULL, choices = c("Slope b" = "beta", "R\u00b2" = "r2"),
                     selected = "beta", inline = TRUE)
      )
    )
  ),

  # Fills the rest of the window; never shorter than min_height (the page scrolls below that)
  layout_columns(
    min_height = "560px",
    col_widths = c(4, 3, 5),
    card(
            card_header(class = "py-1", "1. Our observed dataset"),
      plotOutput("focal"),
      card_footer(class = "small py-1", uiOutput("focal_note"))
    ),
    card(
            card_header(class = "py-1", "2. Four more datasets, same population"),
      plotOutput("grid"),
      card_footer(class = "small py-1", uiOutput("grid_note"))
    ),
    card(
            card_header(class = "py-1", "3. Where does our estimate fall? 100 studies per world"),
      plotOutput("pile_h0"),
      plotOutput("pile_ha"),
      card_footer(class = "small py-1", uiOutput("pile_note"))
    )
  )
)


# ---- Server --------------------------------------------------------------------------

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  rv <- reactiveValues(pile_seed = random_seed())

  observeEvent(input$new_samples, updateNumericInput(session, "seed", value = random_seed()))
  observeEvent(input$new_piles, rv$pile_seed <- random_seed())

  x_val <- reactive({ req(input$x_var); input$x_var })
  y_val <- reactive(outcome_of(x_val(), input$y_var))
  n_val <- reactive(as.integer(input$n))

  # The outcome box is always shown. With a test as predictor it holds only the other test;
  # with gender it offers both tests (keeping the current choice).
  observeEvent(input$x_var, {
    ch <- y_choices(input$x_var)
    updateSelectInput(session, "y_var", choices = ch,
                      selected = if (input$y_var %in% ch && lm_is_binary(input$x_var)) input$y_var else
                        if (lm_is_binary(input$x_var)) ch[[1]] else lm_other_var(input$x_var))
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  output$slider_title <- renderText(slider_label(x_val(), input$units))

  # Changing the predictor, the outcome (gender only) or the units re-ranges the slider
  # (units and limits change). Keep the same standardised slope rather than the same number.
  prev <- reactiveValues(x = x_default, y = y_default, units = "raw")
  observeEvent(list(input$x_var, input$y_var, input$units), {
    x <- input$x_var; y <- outcome_of(x, input$y_var)
    req(x != y)
    if (identical(prev$x, x) && identical(prev$y, y) && identical(prev$units, input$units)) return()
    r_keep <- if (prev$units == "std") input$beta else lm_beta_to_r(input$beta, prev$x, prev$y)
    if (input$units == "std") {
      lim <- std_slider_limit()
      updateSliderInput(session, "beta",
                        min = -lim, max = lim, step = 0.05,
                        value = max(-lim, min(lim, round(r_keep * 20) / 20)))
    } else {
      lim <- lm_slope_limit(x, y); st <- lm_slope_step(x)
      v <- round(round(lm_r_to_beta(r_keep, x, y) / st) * st, 2)
      updateSliderInput(session, "beta", min = -lim, max = lim,
                        step = st, value = max(-lim, min(lim, v)))
    }
    prev$x <- x; prev$y <- y; prev$units <- input$units
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  seed_val <- reactive({
    s <- input$seed
    validate(need(!is.null(s) && !is.na(s) && s >= 1 && s <= 10000 && s == round(s),
                  "Seed must be a whole number from 1 to 10000."))
    as.integer(s)
  })

  # The slider's value is in the chosen units; internally everything uses the raw slope.
  # While the slider is being re-ranged its value can briefly lie outside the new range
  # (or in the old units); wait for the update rather than simulate an impossible r.
  beta_val <- reactive({
    v <- input$beta
    req(!is.null(v), input$units %in% c("raw", "std"))
    lim <- if (input$units == "std") std_slider_limit() else lm_slope_limit(x_val(), y_val())
    req(abs(v) <= lim + 1e-9)
    if (input$units == "std") lm_r_to_beta(v, x_val(), y_val()) else v
  })

  # cache = "session": the same app.R also runs as a static shinylive page
  fg <- reactive(simulate_lm_focal_and_grid(n_val(), beta_val(), x_val(), y_val(), seed_val())) |>
    bindCache(n_val(), beta_val(), x_val(), y_val(), seed_val(), cache = "session")

  piles <- reactive(simulate_lm_piles(n_val(), beta_val(), x_val(), y_val(), rv$pile_seed)) |>
    bindCache(n_val(), beta_val(), x_val(), y_val(), rv$pile_seed, cache = "session")

  pile_for_app <- function(world) {
    # Skip the very first draw, before the browser has given the plot a size
    h <- session$clientData[[paste0("output_pile_", world, "_height")]]
    req(!is.null(h), h > 30)
    w <- session$clientData[[paste0("output_pile_", world, "_width")]]
    # Plotting-panel size = plot size minus the title / subtitle / axis space; sets the dot size
    plot_lm_pile(piles(), world, input$stat, fg()$focal_stats, zoom = input$zoom, units = input$units,
                 panel_px = c(max(w - 50, 200), max(h - 100, 50))) +
      theme(legend.position = "none",
            plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
            plot.margin = margin(5.5, 10, 14, 5.5))
  }

  output$focal <- renderPlot(plot_lm_focal(fg(), input$units), res = 96)
  output$grid  <- renderPlot(plot_lm_grid(fg(), input$units), res = 96)
  output$pile_h0 <- renderPlot(pile_for_app("h0"), res = 96)
  output$pile_ha <- renderPlot(pile_for_app("ha"), res = 96)

  # Model formula
  output$model_note <- renderUI(span(lm_var_label(y_val()), " ~ ", lm_var_label(x_val())))

  output$focal_note <- renderUI({
    r <- lm_beta_to_r(beta_val(), x_val(), y_val())
    if (lm_is_binary(x_val())) {
      helpText(sprintf(paste("HA world: population mean difference b = %.1f points (M - F; F is the",
                             "reference group, coded 0), i.e. Cohen's d = %.2f, point-biserial r = standardised",
                             "beta = %.2f (%s), population R\u00b2 = %.2f; N = %d (equal groups).",
                             "Same t and p as the equal-variance two-sample t test."),
                       beta_val(), 2 * r / sqrt(1 - r^2), r, r_size_label(r), r^2, n_val()))
    } else {
      helpText(sprintf(paste("HA world: population slope b = %.2f (raw units), i.e. standardised beta = r = %.2f",
                             "(%s) and population R\u00b2 = %.2f; N = %d. Same t and p as the test of r."),
                       beta_val(), r, r_size_label(r), r^2, n_val()))
    }
  })

  output$grid_note <- renderUI({
    helpText("Same population slope, same N, independent samples: each gives a different b and R\u00b2.")
  })

  output$pile_note <- renderUI({
    base <- tagList(
      span(style = "color:#0072B2; font-weight:bold", "Blue"), ": not significant; ",
      span(style = "color:#E69F00; font-weight:bold", "orange"), ": significant. ",
      "Dashed: critical value (approximate: each study's own SE differs; colours use its exact p). ",
      span(style = "font-weight:bold", "Solid black line"), ": our observed value (dotted: true value).")
    extra <- if (input$stat == "r2") {
      paste("R\u00b2 cannot be negative, so even under H0 it averages about 1/(N-1), not 0;",
            "the significance test is two-sided in b but one line in R\u00b2.")
    } else if (abs(beta_val()) < 1e-9) {
      "At b = 0, H0 and HA describe the same population, so both piles are draws from it."
    } else NULL
    helpText(base, extra)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

name: nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R
content:
#' ============================================================
#' nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R
#'
#' Demonstration figures contrasting Fisher's significance-testing
#' framework with Neyman & Pearson's hypothesis-testing framework, for the
#' hypothesis-testing-significance.qmd lecture. Built entirely on top of
#' psych-battery-dgp.R's `simulate_pair()`/`run_sweep()`, using one focal
#' pair throughout:
#'
#'   StuVoc1 (vocabulary, 50 items)  --  ART3 (print exposure, 90 items)
#'   Vermeiren-default observed r = .52 (default_r_obs_matrix())
#'
#' The lecture simulates this pair under two worlds:
#'   H0 true: true_corr = 0   (vocabulary and print exposure are unrelated)
#'   H1 true: true_corr = .5  (close to the Vermeiren-default .52)
#'
#' A single sample size, N = 30, is used for every *fixed-N* demonstration
#' (both the Fisher "suppose H0 is true" demos and the Neyman-Pearson
#' H0-true/H1-true demos) -- chosen because it is close to the sample size
#' needed for power = .80 at r = .5, alpha = .05 two-sided
#' (pwr::pwr.r.test(r = .5, sig.level = .05, power = .8) gives n \u2248 28.2;
#' the empirical power of this script's own DGP at n = 30 is \u2248 .82, see
#' the walkthrough). Using the *same* N for both worlds is deliberate: it
#' keeps "what changed?" unambiguous (only the true correlation), and it's
#' also statistically apt, since the empirical false-positive rate under
#' H0 doesn't depend on N -- alpha is a property of the decision rule, not
#' of the sample. Only the "funnel"/corridor demonstrations, which are
#' specifically about the effect of varying N, use N = 50/100/1000.
#'
#' Significance is encoded by colour alone throughout (no point shape),
#' using the Okabe-Ito colour-blind-safe pair already used by
#' person-grid.R: "#0072B2" (blue) = not significant, "#E69F00" (orange)
#' = significant.
#'
#' Requires: psych-battery-dgp.R sourced first (uses simulate_pair(),
#' fit_focal_cor(), run_sweep(), default_r_obs_matrix()); ggplot2; ggdist.
#'
#' Quarto usage:
#'   ```{r}
#'   source("psych-battery-dgp.R")
#'   source("nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R")
#'
#'   # Fisher section: one grid of 6 studies, H0 true, n = 30
#'   studies <- simulate_many_studies(n = 30, n_studies = 6, true_corr = 0, seed = 11)
#'   plot_scatter_grid(studies, "ART3", "StuVoc1")
#'
#'   # ... and the same 6 studies' r / t values as dot-piles
#'   fits <- fit_many_studies(studies, "ART3", "StuVoc1")
#'   plot_dotpile_stat(fits$estimate, xlab = "r")
#'   plot_dotpile_stat(t_from_r(fits$estimate, n = 30), xlab = "t",
#'                      vline = critical_t(30), vline_label = "critical t (alpha = .05)")
#'
#'   # Neyman-Pearson section: 1000 studies, H1 true, n = 30
#'   sweep <- run_sweep(n_grid = 30, true_corr_grid = .5, reps = 1000,
#'                       var_x = "StuVoc1", var_y = "ART3", seed_base = 22)
#'   plot_dotpile_significance(sweep$estimate, xlab = "r", significant = sweep$significant,
#'                              vlines = c(`critical r` = critical_r(30), `true r` = .5))
#'
#'   # Funnel plots: same effect, varying N
#'   plot_funnel("StuVoc1", "ART3", n_grid = c(50, 100, 1000), true_corr = .5, reps = 300, seed_base = 33)
#'   plot_funnel_multi_effect("StuVoc1", "ART3", n_grid = c(50, 100, 1000),
#'                             true_corr_grid = c(.25, .5, .75), reps = 300, seed_base = 44)
#'   ```
#' ============================================================

library(ggplot2)

# ---- significance palette (Okabe-Ito, colour-blind-safe; colour-only, no shape) ----

sig_colors <- c("not significant" = "#0072B2", "significant" = "#E69F00")

#' Turn a logical "significant" vector into the labelled factor used by
#' every colour-by-significance plot in this script, so the legend
#' wording and factor level order are identical everywhere.
significance_label <- function(significant) {
  factor(significant, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE), labels = c("not significant", "significant"))
}

# ---- r / t / critical-value helpers ----------------------------------------

#' The t-statistic for a Pearson correlation, given r and sample size n.
#' t = r * sqrt(n - 2) / sqrt(1 - r^2); see fit_focal_cor()/cor.test() for
#' the version computed directly from data -- this is the same formula,
#' applied to an already-computed r (e.g. from run_sweep()'s output).
t_from_r <- function(r, n) {
  r * sqrt(n - 2) / sqrt(1 - r^2)
}

#' The critical two-sided t-value for a Pearson correlation test with
#' n - 2 degrees of freedom.
critical_t <- function(n, alpha = 0.05) {
  stopifnot("`n` must be at least 3" = n >= 3)
  qt(1 - alpha / 2, df = n - 2)
}

#' The critical two-sided |r| boundary at sample size n -- the observed r
#' at which the t-test for that correlation exactly reaches the critical
#' t. Inverts t_from_r() algebraically: r_crit = t_crit / sqrt(t_crit^2 + n - 2).
critical_r <- function(n, alpha = 0.05) {
  tcrit <- critical_t(n, alpha)
  tcrit / sqrt(tcrit^2 + n - 2)
}

# ---- simulating small grids of studies (for scatter grids / small dot-piles) ----

#' Simulate `n_studies` independent studies of `n` participants each, all
#' drawn from the same (var_x, var_y) population correlation -- the small-
#' n_studies analogue of run_sweep(), returning the *raw* per-person data
#' (not just fitted estimates), for scatter-grid figures.
#'
#' @param n            participants per study.
#' @param n_studies    number of independent studies.
#' @param true_corr    population *observed*-score correlation to simulate
#'                      from (see simulate_pair()'s corr_scale argument).
#' @param var_x, var_y the focal pair of tests.
#' @param reliability  reliability override applied to both tests; NULL
#'                      (default) uses each test's Vermeiren-default value.
#' @param corr_scale   "observed" (default) or "latent"; passed through to
#'                      simulate_pair().
#' @param seed         base seed; study s uses seed + s, so each study is
#'                      independently drawn but the whole grid is
#'                      reproducible.
#' @return a long data frame: `study` (factor, "Study 1" .. "Study n_studies"),
#'   plus the `var_x`/`var_y` score columns from simulate_pair().
simulate_many_studies <- function(n, n_studies, true_corr = 0, var_x = "StuVoc1", var_y = "ART3",
                                   reliability = NULL, corr_scale = c("observed", "latent"), seed = NULL) {
  corr_scale <- match.arg(corr_scale)
  panels <- vector("list", n_studies)
  for (s in seq_len(n_studies)) {
    seed_s <- if (is.null(seed)) NULL else seed + s
    d <- simulate_pair(n, var_x, var_y, true_corr = true_corr, corr_scale = corr_scale,
                        reliability_x = reliability, reliability_y = reliability, seed = seed_s)
    d$study <- sprintf("Study %d", s)
    panels[[s]] <- d
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, panels)
  out$study <- factor(out$study, levels = sprintf("Study %d", seq_len(n_studies)))
  out
}

#' Fit a Pearson correlation test within each `study` of a
#' simulate_many_studies()-style data frame, returning one row per study.
#'
#' @param data           a data frame with a `study` column (as returned
#'                         by simulate_many_studies()).
#' @param var_x, var_y   the focal pair of tests.
#' @param alpha          significance threshold.
#' @return a data frame: `study`, `estimate`, `ci_low`, `ci_high`,
#'   `p_value`, `significant`.
fit_many_studies <- function(data, var_x, var_y, alpha = 0.05) {
  studies <- levels(droplevels(data$study))
  rows <- lapply(studies, function(s) {
    fit <- fit_focal_cor(data[data$study == s, , drop = FALSE], var_x, var_y)
    cbind(study = s, fit, significant = fit$p_value < alpha)
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  out$study <- factor(out$study, levels = studies)
  out
}

# ---- scatter grid -----------------------------------------------------------

#' A facet_wrap(~study) grid of scatterplots, one panel per simulated
#' study -- shared theme/colour with the rest of the project's raw-data
#' scatterplots (plain blue points, no significance encoding: this is
#' "what the data look like", before any test is applied).
#'
#' @param data            a data frame with a `study` column (as returned
#'                          by simulate_many_studies()).
#' @param var_x, var_y    the focal pair of tests (column names in `data`).
#' @param ncol            panels per row.
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_scatter_grid <- function(data, var_x, var_y, ncol = 3) {
  ggplot(data, aes(.data[[var_x]], .data[[var_y]])) +
    geom_point(color = "#3B6EA5", alpha = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = ncol) +
    labs(x = var_x, y = var_y) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

# ---- dot-piles: a statistic's distribution, with and without significance ----

#' A sensible default dot diameter (in data units) for ggdist::stat_dots(),
#' used whenever a dot-pile function's `binwidth` argument is left NULL.
#'
#' ggdist's own auto-binwidth (`binwidth = NA`) is tuned for the "many
#' points, one panel" case and works well there (verified up to n = 1000
#' for this script's r/t-value ranges), but for a *handful* of points
#' (e.g. the six-study demonstrations) it tends to pick a binwidth coarse
#' enough that distinct-but-nearby values get treated as ties and nudged
#' sideways into overlapping "petal" clusters rather than cleanly stacked
#' points. Below a small-n threshold, this instead scales the binwidth
#' directly off the data's own range and n, which keeps genuinely distinct
#' values visually separate while still stacking true (or near-)ties.
#' Above the threshold, ggdist's own auto-binwidth (`NA`) is used
#' unchanged.
#'
#' @param values  the numeric vector that will be plotted.
#' @return a single numeric binwidth, or `NA` (ggdist's own "auto").
default_dotpile_binwidth <- function(values) {
  n <- length(values)
  if (n <= 20) diff(range(values)) / (3 * n) else NA
}

#' Manually stack a small number of values into dot-pile-style (x, y)
#' positions, grouping each value with its neighbour into the same column
#' whenever they're within `binwidth` of each other (greedy, after
#' sorting). This exists only so that individual points can be labelled
#' exactly: `ggdist::stat_dots()`'s own stacking is computed at draw time
#' in grid units and isn't recoverable from `ggplot_build()`, so exact
#' per-point label placement (`plot_dotpile_labeled()`) isn't otherwise
#' possible. Intended for the same small-n regime as
#' `default_dotpile_binwidth()`'s n <= 20 branch -- not a general
#' replacement for ggdist's own layout.
#'
#' @param values     numeric vector to position.
#' @param binwidth   grouping tolerance; NULL (default) picks
#'                     `default_dotpile_binwidth()`.
#' @return a data frame: `x` (sorted values), `y` (stack level within its
#'   column, starting at 0), `order` (the index into the original
#'   `values` that each row corresponds to, for attaching per-point
#'   labels/colours after sorting).
stack_dot_positions <- function(values, binwidth = NULL) {
  if (is.null(binwidth) || is.na(binwidth)) binwidth <- default_dotpile_binwidth(values)
  if (is.na(binwidth)) binwidth <- diff(range(values)) / 30
  ord <- order(values)
  x <- values[ord]
  y <- integer(length(x))
  level <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(x)) {
    if (i == 1 || (x[i] - x[i - 1]) > binwidth) level <- 0 else level <- level + 1
    y[i] <- level
  }
  data.frame(x = x, y = y, order = ord)
}

#' A dot-pile with each point labelled (e.g. by study number), built on
#' `stack_dot_positions()` rather than `ggdist::stat_dots()` so that
#' labels land exactly on their point -- intended for small `n` (e.g. the
#' six-study demonstrations), where identifying which point came from
#' which study is pedagogically useful.
#'
#' @param values        numeric vector (r or t values, one per study).
#' @param labels         vector the same length as `values` (e.g. study
#'                         numbers) to print inside each dot.
#' @param xlab          x-axis label, e.g. "r" or "t".
#' @param vline         optional single reference value to draw as a
#'                        dotted vertical line.
#' @param vline_label    optional short label placed near the top of
#'                        `vline`.
#' @param binwidth       grouping tolerance; NULL (default) picks
#'                         `default_dotpile_binwidth()`.
#' @param dot_size, text_size  point size and label text size.
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_dotpile_labeled <- function(values, labels, xlab, vline = NULL, vline_label = NULL,
                                  binwidth = NULL, dot_size = 11, text_size = 3) {
  pos <- stack_dot_positions(values, binwidth)
  pos$label <- labels[pos$order]
  p <- ggplot(pos, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
    geom_point(size = dot_size, color = "#0072B2") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), color = "white", size = text_size, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_x_continuous(name = xlab) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.6, max(pos$y) + 0.6)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black"))
  if (!is.null(vline)) {
    full_range <- range(c(values, vline))
    hjust <- if (vline > mean(full_range)) 1.05 else -0.05
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = vline, color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted")
    if (!is.null(vline_label)) {
      p <- p + annotate("text", x = vline, y = Inf, label = vline_label,
                         vjust = 1.5, hjust = hjust, size = 3, color = "gray40")
    }
  }
  p
}

#' A single-colour "pile of dots" (ggdist::stat_dots) showing the
#' distribution of a statistic (r or t) across simulated studies, with no
#' significance encoding -- used for Fisher-style demonstrations, which
#' never classify an individual result as "significant"/"not significant"
#' (that distinction belongs to Neyman-Pearson).
#'
#' @param values        numeric vector (r or t values, one per study).
#' @param xlab          x-axis label, e.g. "r" or "t".
#' @param vline         optional single reference value (e.g. a critical
#'                        t, or one highlighted "observed" value) to draw
#'                        as a dotted vertical line.
#' @param vline_label    optional short label placed near the top of
#'                        `vline`, annotating what it represents.
#' @param binwidth       dot diameter in data units; NULL (default) picks
#'                        `default_dotpile_binwidth()`.
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_dotpile_stat <- function(values, xlab, vline = NULL, vline_label = NULL, binwidth = NULL) {
  if (!requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile_stat(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').")
  }
  if (is.null(binwidth)) binwidth <- default_dotpile_binwidth(values)
  df <- data.frame(value = values)
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = value)) +
    ggdist::stat_dots(color = "#0072B2", fill = "#0072B2", binwidth = binwidth) +
    scale_x_continuous(name = xlab) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black"))
  if (!is.null(vline)) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = vline, color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted")
    if (!is.null(vline_label)) {
      # Right-align (and tuck inside the panel) labels whose line sits in
      # the right half of the plotted range, so the label text can't run
      # off the right edge; left-align (as before) otherwise.
      full_range <- range(c(values, vline))
      hjust <- if (vline > mean(full_range)) 1.05 else -0.05
      p <- p + annotate("text", x = vline, y = Inf, label = vline_label,
                         vjust = 1.5, hjust = hjust, size = 3, color = "gray40")
    }
  }
  p
}

#' As plot_dotpile_stat(), but coloured by significance (Okabe-Ito pair,
#' colour only -- no shape), with one or more labelled reference lines
#' (e.g. the critical r boundary and/or the true population r) -- used
#' for every Neyman-Pearson-section dot-pile.
#'
#' @param values        numeric vector (r values, one per study).
#' @param xlab          x-axis label.
#' @param significant   logical vector, same length as `values`.
#' @param vlines        optional named numeric vector of reference values,
#'                        e.g. c(`critical r` = .31, `true r` = .5); names
#'                        are used as labels.
#' @param binwidth       dot diameter in data units; NULL (default) picks
#'                        `default_dotpile_binwidth()`.
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_dotpile_significance <- function(values, xlab, significant, vlines = NULL, binwidth = NULL) {
  if (!requireNamespace("ggdist", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("Package 'ggdist' is required for plot_dotpile_significance(). Install with install.packages('ggdist').")
  }
  if (is.null(binwidth)) binwidth <- default_dotpile_binwidth(values)
  df <- data.frame(value = values, significant_label = significance_label(significant))
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = value, color = significant_label, fill = significant_label)) +
    ggdist::stat_dots(binwidth = binwidth) +
    scale_color_manual(values = sig_colors, name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = sig_colors, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(name = xlab) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          axis.line.x = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(color = "black"))
  if (!is.null(vlines)) {
    # Order by position, so staggered vjust steps always run low-x-to-
    # high-x; right-align labels on the right half of the range (so their
    # text tucks back into the panel instead of running off the edge),
    # and stagger each label's vjust so two reference lines close enough
    # in x that their labels would otherwise collide (e.g. critical r and
    # true r sitting a few hundredths of r apart) are stacked instead.
    ord <- order(vlines)
    vline_df <- data.frame(x = unname(vlines)[ord], label = names(vlines)[ord])
    full_range <- range(c(values, vlines))
    vline_df$hjust <- ifelse(vline_df$x > mean(full_range), 1.05, -0.05)
    vline_df$vjust <- 1.5 + 1.5 * (seq_len(nrow(vline_df)) - 1)
    p <- p + geom_vline(data = vline_df, aes(xintercept = x), color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted",
                         inherit.aes = FALSE)
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(vline_df))) {
      p <- p + annotate("text", x = vline_df$x[i], y = Inf, label = vline_df$label[i],
                         vjust = vline_df$vjust[i], hjust = vline_df$hjust[i],
                         size = 3, color = "gray40")
    }
  }
  p
}

# ---- funnel / corridor plots: one effect, many n -----------------------------

#' A "funnel"/corridor plot for one fixed population correlation, one
#' panel per sample size -- each panel shows run_sweep()'s replicate
#' studies at that n as jittered points (x = observed r), coloured by
#' significance, with that panel's own critical-r boundary and a vline at
#' the true population r. Panels are faceted (not stacked on one y-axis,
#' as nhst-power.R's plot_corridor() does) because the critical-r boundary
#' depends on n and needs its own position in each panel.
#'
#' @param var_x, var_y     the focal pair of tests.
#' @param n_grid            sample sizes to compare (one facet panel each).
#' @param true_corr         the single population *observed*-score
#'                           correlation to simulate from (0 for the
#'                           H0-true funnel, e.g. .5 for an H1-true funnel).
#' @param reps              independent studies simulated per sample size.
#' @param reliability       reliability override applied to both tests;
#'                           NULL (default) uses Vermeiren-default values.
#' @param alpha             significance threshold.
#' @param seed_base         base seed, passed through to run_sweep().
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_funnel <- function(var_x, var_y, n_grid, true_corr, reps = 300, reliability = NULL,
                         alpha = 0.05, seed_base = 1234) {
  raw <- run_sweep(n_grid = n_grid, true_corr_grid = true_corr, reliability_grid = reliability,
                    reps = reps, var_x = var_x, var_y = var_y, alpha = alpha, seed_base = seed_base)
  raw$significant_label <- significance_label(raw$significant)
  crit_df <- data.frame(n = n_grid, crit = vapply(n_grid, critical_r, numeric(1), alpha = alpha))

  # Conventional funnel-plot orientation: precision (n) increasing upward,
  # so the narrow, high-precision studies sit at the top and the wide,
  # more variable small-n studies sit at the bottom.
  n_levels <- sort(unique(n_grid), decreasing = TRUE)
  raw$n <- factor(raw$n, levels = n_levels)
  crit_df$n <- factor(crit_df$n, levels = n_levels)

  ggplot(raw, aes(x = estimate, y = 0, color = significant_label)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = true_corr, color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_vline(data = crit_df, aes(xintercept = crit), color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(data = crit_df, aes(xintercept = -crit), color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_jitter(height = 0.3, alpha = 0.6, size = 2.2) +
    scale_color_manual(values = sig_colors, name = NULL) +
    facet_wrap(~ n, ncol = 1, labeller = label_both) +
    labs(x = sprintf("Observed r(%s, %s)", var_x, var_y),
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%d simulated studies per n; true (population) correlation = %.2f (dotted); dashed lines = +/- critical r at alpha = %.2f",
           reps, true_corr, alpha)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

#' As plot_funnel(), but for several population correlations at once --
#' faceted on a 2-D grid of n x true_corr (rows x columns), so true_corr
#' doesn't have to be double-encoded through colour (colour is already
#' spent on significance).
#'
#' @inheritParams plot_funnel
#' @param true_corr_grid  population *observed*-score correlations to
#'                         compare, e.g. c(.25, .5, .75).
#' @return a ggplot object.
plot_funnel_multi_effect <- function(var_x, var_y, n_grid, true_corr_grid, reps = 300,
                                      reliability = NULL, alpha = 0.05, seed_base = 1234) {
  raw <- run_sweep(n_grid = n_grid, true_corr_grid = true_corr_grid, reliability_grid = reliability,
                    reps = reps, var_x = var_x, var_y = var_y, alpha = alpha, seed_base = seed_base)
  raw$significant_label <- significance_label(raw$significant)

  crit_df <- expand.grid(n = n_grid, true_corr = true_corr_grid)
  crit_df$crit <- vapply(crit_df$n, critical_r, numeric(1), alpha = alpha)
  true_df <- data.frame(true_corr = true_corr_grid)

  # Conventional funnel-plot orientation: precision (n) increasing upward.
  n_levels <- sort(unique(n_grid), decreasing = TRUE)
  raw$n <- factor(raw$n, levels = n_levels)
  crit_df$n <- factor(crit_df$n, levels = n_levels)

  ggplot(raw, aes(x = estimate, y = 0, color = significant_label)) +
    geom_vline(data = true_df, aes(xintercept = true_corr), color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(data = crit_df, aes(xintercept = crit), color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_vline(data = crit_df, aes(xintercept = -crit), color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    geom_jitter(height = 0.3, alpha = 0.5, size = 0.9) +
    scale_color_manual(values = sig_colors, name = NULL) +
    facet_grid(n ~ true_corr,
               labeller = labeller(n = label_both, true_corr = function(x) paste0("true r: ", x))) +
    labs(x = sprintf("Observed r(%s, %s)", var_x, var_y),
         subtitle = sprintf(
           "%d simulated studies per cell; dotted line = true (population) correlation; dashed lines = +/- critical r at alpha = %.2f",
           reps, alpha)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
}

#' ============================================================
#' nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b.R   (VERSION B: one predictor)
#'
#' Shiny-free helpers behind VERSION B of the linear-model sampling-variability
#' app (nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b-app/app.R). Same idea as the correlation
#' app (nhst-sampling-variability.R), but the statistic is the slope b1 (and R^2)
#' of the simple linear model
#'
#'     y = b0 + b1 * x + error
#'
#' where x and y are two of the project's tests (reading experience = ART3,
#' vocabulary = StuVoc1), in RAW score units.
#'
#'   column 1: the observed ("focal") dataset: scatterplot + geom_smooth(lm)
#'   column 2: four more datasets from the same population (same slope, same N)
#'   column 3: two piles of dots, 100 studies each: H0 true (slope = 0, upper)
#'             and HA true (slope = the slider, lower); dots blue = not
#'             significant, orange = significant
#'
#' PHASE A: one continuous predictor (reading experience or vocabulary).
#' PHASE B: gender (M vs F) as a binary predictor, same file. The slope is then
#' the M - F mean difference (F = reference, coded 0; M = 1).
#'
#' This file is Version B only: it is the current Version C helper file
#' (nhst-sampling-variability-lm.R) with the Phase C features removed (age, adjusting
#' for other predictors, added-variable plots, added R^2, VIF). Function names are the
#' same as in Version C, so DO NOT source both files into one R session. With no
#' other predictors ticked, Version C gives identical results (checked by a parity
#' script; see nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b-walkthrough.qmd).
#'
#' Why this can reuse the correlation machinery. In simple regression the t-test
#' of b1 is the same test as the t-test of r (same t, df and p), and R^2 = r^2.
#' So the population is still simulated with simulate_pair() at a population
#' correlation r = b1 * sd(x) / sd(y); what is new is the estimation of b1 and
#' the conversion between slope and correlation.
#'
#' Built on, and modifying none of:
#'   psych-battery-dgp.R: simulate_pair(), get_calibration(), default_*()
#'   nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R: simulate_many_studies(),
#'     plot_scatter_grid(), plot_dotpile_significance(), critical_r()
#'   nhst-sampling-variability.R: expected_power(), format_p(), r_size_label(),
#'     sv_n_choices, sv_r_limits, sv_point_color
#'
#' Seeds: focal = master seed, four-grid = master + 20000 (+ study number),
#' piles >= 1e6 (see simulate_lm_piles()), so none can coincide.
#'
#' Known approximations (documented in the walkthrough):
#'  * The "true slope" is NOMINAL: it is converted to a population r using the
#'    model-implied SDs, but the realised observed r runs a few per cent below
#'    nominal (linear disattenuation applied to a nonlinear item model).
#'  * The dashed "critical slope" lines use population SDs; each study's
#'    exact critical slope is t_crit * its own SE, which varies from study to
#'    study. Dot colours always use each study's exact p.
#'
#' Console usage:
#'   ```{r}
#'   source("psych-battery-dgp.R")
#'   source("nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R")
#'   source("nhst-sampling-variability.R")
#'   source("nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b.R")
#'   fg <- simulate_lm_focal_and_grid(n = 30, beta = .2, x = "ART3", y = "StuVoc1", seed = 1)
#'   pl <- simulate_lm_piles(n = 30, beta = .2, x = "ART3", y = "StuVoc1", pile_seed = 1)
#'   plot_lm_focal(fg)
#'   plot_lm_grid(fg)
#'   plot_lm_pile(pl, "h0", "beta", fg$focal_stats)
#'   plot_lm_pile(pl, "ha", "r2", fg$focal_stats)
#'   ```
#' ============================================================

library(ggplot2)

# ---- variables --------------------------------------------------------------------

#' The two continuous predictors/outcomes (the two tests), as
#' label = column name (the labels are what the app's drop-down shows).
lm_var_choices <- c("Reading experience" = "ART3", "Vocabulary" = "StuVoc1")

#' Predictor choices: the two tests and gender (binary: F = 0 reference, M = 1).
lm_x_choices <- c(lm_var_choices, "Gender (M vs F)" = "gender")

#' TRUE for the binary predictor.
lm_is_binary <- function(v) identical(v, "gender")

#' Plain-language label for a column name.
lm_var_label <- function(v) names(lm_x_choices)[match(v, lm_x_choices)]

#' Score range of each test (50 and 90 items), fixed so panels and redraws are
#' comparable.
lm_var_limits <- list(ART3 = c(0, 90), StuVoc1 = c(0, 50))

#' The other variable of the pair (there are exactly two tests).
lm_other_var <- function(v) setdiff(unname(lm_var_choices), v)

#' Population SD of a test's observed score, from the calibrated item model
#' (the same machinery simulate_pair() uses), so slope <-> r conversions need
#' no simulation.
lm_pop_sd <- function(v) {
  # Gender: two exactly equal groups coded 0/1 -> population SD 0.5. With this,
  # r = b * sd_x / sd_y gives r = (M - F difference) / (2 * sd_y), the equal-groups
  # point-biserial correlation, so every slope <-> r function below works unchanged.
  if (lm_is_binary(v)) return(0.5)
  sp  <- default_test_specs()[[v]]
  rel <- default_reliability_vec()[[v]]
  get_calibration(sp$mu, rel, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)$moments$sd_total
}

# ---- slope <-> correlation ------------------------------------------------------------

#' Nominal population correlation for a population slope of y on x:
#' r = b1 * sd(x) / sd(y).
lm_beta_to_r <- function(beta, x, y) beta * lm_pop_sd(x) / lm_pop_sd(y)

#' Inverse: b1 = r * sd(y) / sd(x), in units of y per unit of x.
lm_r_to_beta <- function(r, x, y) r * lm_pop_sd(y) / lm_pop_sd(x)

#' Slider step in raw units: 0.01 for the tests, 0.1 score points for the
#' (much larger) gender mean difference.
lm_slope_step <- function(x) if (lm_is_binary(x)) 0.1 else 0.01

#' Largest |slope| the slider offers: the slope that corresponds to the
#' population-r cap `sv_r_limits[2]` (.85; attenuation ceiling), rounded down
#' to the slider's step.
lm_slope_limit <- function(x, y) {
  st <- lm_slope_step(x)
  round(floor(lm_r_to_beta(sv_r_limits[2], x, y) / st + 1e-9) * st, 2)
}

#' The slope that corresponds to r = 1 (x-axis half-width of the full-range
#' slope pile).
lm_slope_scale <- function(x, y) lm_r_to_beta(1, x, y)

# ---- estimation --------------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Slope, SE, t, df, exact two-sided p and R^2 of the simple regression of y on x
#' (closed form; identical to summary(lm(y ~ x)), checked in the tests).
#'
#' @return one-row data frame: `beta`, `se` (raw units), `beta_std`, `se_std`
#'   (standardised slope = r, and its SE, from the sample SDs), `t`, `df`, `p`,
#'   `r2`, `significant`.
slope_stats <- function(x, y, alpha = 0.05) {
  n   <- length(x)
  sxx <- sum((x - mean(x))^2)
  sxy <- sum((x - mean(x)) * (y - mean(y)))
  syy <- sum((y - mean(y))^2)
  b   <- sxy / sxx
  r2  <- sxy^2 / (sxx * syy)
  se  <- sqrt(syy * (1 - r2) / (n - 2) / sxx)
  t   <- b / se
  p   <- 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t), n - 2)
  data.frame(beta = b, se = se, beta_std = sxy / sqrt(sxx * syy), se_std = se * sqrt(sxx / syy),
             t = t, df = n - 2, p = p, r2 = r2, significant = p < alpha)
}

#' Name used for the slope in labels: "b" (raw units) or "beta" (standardised;
#' spelled out, not a Greek letter, so it renders in any font, including webR).
lm_sym <- function(units) if (identical(units, "std")) "beta" else "b"

#' "b = 0.21 (SE 0.09), t(28) = 2.34, p = .027, R^2 = .16" (this order); with
#' `two_lines = TRUE` the line breaks after t(df) (for the narrow focal panel).
#' `units` = "raw" or "std".
lm_stat_label <- function(s, with_p = TRUE, two_lines = FALSE, units = "raw") {
  std <- identical(units, "std")
  r2  <- lm_r2_text(s)
  est <- sprintf("%s = %.2f (SE %.2f), t(%d) = %.2f", lm_sym(units), if (std) s$beta_std else s$beta,
                 if (std) s$se_std else s$se, as.integer(s$df), s$t)
  tail <- if (with_p) paste(format_p(s$p), r2, sep = ", ") else r2
  paste0(est, if (two_lines) ",\n" else ", ", tail)
}

#' R^2 text: "R^2 = .16" (leading zero dropped).
lm_r2_text <- function(s) sub("= 0\\.", "= .", sprintf("R\u00b2 = %.2f", s$r2))

#' Wording for a slope: direction and the Cohen-benchmark size of its
#' standardised version (= r).
lm_beta_label <- function(beta, x, y) r_size_label(lm_beta_to_r(beta, x, y))

# ---- simulation ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Observed test scores from latent standardised abilities `z`: the same item
#' model simulate_pair() applies (logistic item curve, guessing floor, binomial
#' item noise), written out so a latent z built any way can be scored.
lm_item_scores <- function(z, var, reliability = default_reliability_vec()[[var]]) {
  n   <- length(z)
  sp  <- default_test_specs()[[var]]
  cal <- get_calibration(sp$mu, reliability, sp$n_items, sp$guessing)
  p   <- sp$guessing + (1 - sp$guessing) * plogis(cal$theta_mu + cal$theta_sigma * z)
  if (identical(var, "ART3")) {
    rbinom(n, sp$split[["authors"]], p) + rbinom(n, sp$split[["foils"]], p)
  } else {
    rbinom(n, sp$n_items, p)
  }
}

#' Simulate `n` people with gender (balanced groups) and one test score.
#'
#' Gender is coded F = 0 (reference), M = 1 and the groups are exactly equal
#' (n / 2 each; for odd n the extra person is F), so group sizes add no noise.
#' The outcome's latent ability is z = b * g + sqrt(1 - b^2) * e, with g = -1 / +1
#' (unit population variance) and e ~ N(0, 1); gender has no measurement error,
#' so the latent b is the target observed correlation divided by sqrt(reliability).
#' As with simulate_pair(), the TOTAL variance of the outcome is held fixed and
#' only the correlation changes.
#'
#' @param r  target observed-score (point-biserial) correlation between gender and `y`.
#' @return a data frame with columns `gender` (0 / 1) and `y`.
lm_simulate_gender <- function(n, r, y, seed = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) set.seed(seed)
  b <- disattenuate(r, 1, default_reliability_vec()[[y]])
  g <- c(rep(0, ceiling(n / 2)), rep(1, floor(n / 2)))
  z <- b * (g - 0.5) / 0.5 + sqrt(1 - b^2) * rnorm(n)
  out <- data.frame(gender = g)
  out[[y]] <- lm_item_scores(z, y)
  out
}

#' One simulated study for any (x, y): a test pair via simulate_pair(), or
#' gender + a test via lm_simulate_gender(). Returns the columns `x` and `y`.
lm_simulate <- function(n, r, x, y, seed = NULL) {
  if (lm_is_binary(x)) return(lm_simulate_gender(n, r, y, seed))
  simulate_pair(n, x, y, true_corr = r, seed = seed)[c(x, y)]
}

#' `n_studies` independent studies (study s uses seed + s, exactly as
#' simulate_many_studies() does, so test pairs are unchanged), as one long data
#' frame with a `study` factor.
lm_simulate_many <- function(n, n_studies, r, x, y, seed) {
  d <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_studies), function(s) {
    cbind(lm_simulate(n, r, x, y, seed + s), study = sprintf("Study %d", s))
  }))
  d$study <- factor(d$study, levels = sprintf("Study %d", seq_len(n_studies)))
  d
}

#' Simulate the focal dataset and the four comparison datasets.
#'
#' @param n,beta,seed  sample size, population slope (raw units; for gender, the M - F
#'   difference), seed.
#' @param x,y          column names (predictor, outcome).
#' @return a list: `n`, `beta`, `r_pop` (the standardised slope = r), `x`, `y`, `focal`
#'   (data frame), `focal_stats` (one row, see slope_stats()), `grid` (long data frame with
#'   a `study` factor), `grid_stats` (one row per study; the strip labels are built in
#'   plot_lm_grid(), so they can follow the units).
simulate_lm_focal_and_grid <- function(n, beta, x, y, seed, alpha = 0.05) {
  r_pop <- lm_beta_to_r(beta, x, y)
  focal <- lm_simulate(n, r_pop, x, y, seed)
  focal_stats <- slope_stats(focal[[x]], focal[[y]], alpha)

  grid <- lm_simulate_many(n, 4, r_pop, x, y, seed + 20000)
  grid_stats <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(grid$study), function(s) {
    g <- grid[grid$study == s, ]
    cbind(study = s, slope_stats(g[[x]], g[[y]], alpha))
  }))
  list(n = n, beta = beta, r_pop = r_pop, x = x, y = y, focal = focal,
       focal_stats = focal_stats, grid = grid, grid_stats = grid_stats)
}

#' Simulate the two 100-study piles: H0 true (population slope 0) and HA true (population
#' slope `beta`), both at sample size `n`.
#'
#' Seed design: study `i` of a world uses
#' `pile_seed + offset + i*1e6 + n*1e3`, with offset 0 (H0) or 12345 (HA). The
#' offset can never be cancelled by the other terms, so no seed is shared
#' between worlds even when beta = 0 (the two piles are then independent draws
#' from the same population). Always >= 1e6, so never equal to a focal/grid seed.
#'
#' @return a list: `n`, `beta`, `r_pop`, `x`, `y`, `alpha`, `h0`, `ha` (one row per study:
#'   slope_stats()), `crit_r`, `crit_beta`, `crit_r2`, `crit_by_world` (approximate critical
#'   values, the same in both worlds, for the slope in raw and standardised units and for
#'   R^2), `true_r2` (the HA world's population R^2), `r2_label`, `expected_h0`, `expected_ha`.
simulate_lm_piles <- function(n, beta, x, y, pile_seed, reps = 100, alpha = 0.05) {
  r_pop <- lm_beta_to_r(beta, x, y)
  one_world <- function(r, offset) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(reps), function(i) {
      d <- lm_simulate(n, r, x, y, pile_seed + offset + i * 1e6 + n * 1e3)
      slope_stats(d[[x]], d[[y]], alpha)
    }))
  }
  crit_r <- critical_r(n, alpha)
  cw <- list(beta = lm_r_to_beta(crit_r, x, y), beta_std = crit_r, r2 = crit_r^2)
  list(n = n, beta = beta, r_pop = r_pop, x = x, y = y, alpha = alpha,
       h0 = one_world(0, 0), ha = one_world(r_pop, 12345),
       crit_r = crit_r, crit_beta = cw$beta, crit_r2 = cw$r2,
       crit_by_world = list(h0 = cw, ha = cw), true_r2 = r_pop^2, r2_label = "R\u00b2",
       expected_h0 = alpha, expected_ha = expected_power(n, r_pop, alpha))
}


# ---- plots ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Colours (colour-blind safe: no red/blue pairing). Points keep the project's
#' blue; the fitted line, its band and the "our observed" marker are near-black,
#' which cannot be confused with the Okabe-Ito blue/orange significance dots.
lm_ink_color <- "#222222"

#' Colour of the fitted line, its confidence band and the group means / CIs:
#' Okabe-Ito bluish green, distinct from the blue points for all common forms of
#' colour-blindness. Each is drawn over a thicker white "halo" so it stays visible
#' against a dense cloud of points (large N).
lm_interval_color <- "#009E73"

#' Point transparency in the focal panel (a little lower than 1 so the fitted line
#' and intervals show through at large N).
lm_focal_alpha <- 0.7

#' The regression line + confidence band drawn on the scatterplots.
lm_smooth <- function(linewidth = 1) {
  list(
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "white",
                linewidth = linewidth + 1.8),
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, color = lm_interval_color, fill = lm_interval_color,
                alpha = 0.15, linewidth = linewidth)
  )
}

#' A text label on a white background (no border) anchored in the headroom of a
#' pile, so dashed/dotted lines never run through the text. ggplot2 4.0 renamed the
#' border argument, so this checks the version (webR may ship an older ggplot2).
lm_label <- function(x, text, vjust, hjust, color) {
  border <- if (utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "4.0.0") list(linewidth = 0) else list(label.size = 0)
  do.call(annotate, c(list("label", x = x, y = Inf, label = text, vjust = vjust, hjust = hjust,
                           size = 3.3, color = color, fill = "white", alpha = 0.9,
                           label.padding = grid::unit(0.12, "lines")), border))
}

#' Group means with 95% t confidence intervals, by `by` columns (e.g. "group", or
#' c("study", "group")).
lm_group_means <- function(d, y, by) {
  keys <- unique(d[by])
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(keys)), function(i) {
    sel <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(by, function(b) d[[b]] == keys[[b]][i]))
    v <- d[[y]][sel]
    m <- mean(v)
    h <- stats::qt(0.975, length(v) - 1) * stats::sd(v) / sqrt(length(v))
    cbind(keys[i, , drop = FALSE], mean = m, lo = m - h, hi = m + h)
  }))
}

#' Layers for a two-group "dot plot": jittered points, the two group means with
#' 95% CIs, and a line joining the means (its slope IS b, the M - F difference).
lm_group_layers <- function(means, y, point_alpha = lm_focal_alpha, point_size = 3) {
  list(
    geom_point(color = sv_point_color, alpha = point_alpha, size = point_size,
               position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 1)),
    geom_errorbar(data = means, aes(y = mean, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.16,
                  color = "white", alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 2.4),
    geom_line(data = means, aes(y = mean, group = 1), color = "white", alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 2.8),
    geom_errorbar(data = means, aes(y = mean, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), width = 0.12,
                  color = lm_interval_color, linewidth = 0.9),
    geom_line(data = means, aes(y = mean, group = 1), color = lm_interval_color, linewidth = 1.1),
    geom_point(data = means, aes(y = mean), color = "white", alpha = 0.6, size = 5, shape = 18),
    geom_point(data = means, aes(y = mean), color = lm_interval_color, size = 3.8, shape = 18),
    scale_y_continuous(limits = lm_var_limits[[y]])
  )
}

#' Gender version of column 1: jittered points by group, group means with 95%
#' CIs and the line joining them; subtitle as in plot_lm_focal().
plot_lm_focal_binary <- function(fg, units = "raw") {
  d <- fg$focal
  d$group <- factor(d[[fg$x]], levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("F", "M"))
  ggplot(d, aes(group, .data[[fg$y]])) +
    lm_group_layers(lm_group_means(d, fg$y, "group"), fg$y) +
    labs(x = "Gender (F = reference, M)", y = lm_var_label(fg$y),
         subtitle = lm_stat_label(fg$focal_stats, two_lines = TRUE, units = units)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
}

#' Strip labels for the four-dataset grid, on three lines: study number; slope
#' (in `units`) and t; R^2.
lm_strip_labels <- function(gs, units = "raw") {
  est <- if (identical(units, "std")) gs$beta_std else gs$beta
  sprintf("%s\n%s = %.2f, t = %.2f\n%s", gs$study, lm_sym(units), est, gs$t,
          vapply(seq_len(nrow(gs)), function(i) lm_r2_text(gs[i, ]), character(1)))
}

#' Gender version of column 2: the four comparison datasets as a 2 x 2 grid.
plot_lm_grid_binary <- function(fg, units = "raw") {
  gs  <- fg$grid_stats
  labels <- lm_strip_labels(gs, units)
  d <- fg$grid
  d$study <- factor(d$study, levels = gs$study, labels = labels)
  d$group <- factor(d[[fg$x]], levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("F", "M"))
  ggplot(d, aes(group, .data[[fg$y]])) +
    lm_group_layers(lm_group_means(d, fg$y, c("study", "group")), fg$y,
                    point_alpha = 0.6, point_size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~study, ncol = 2) +
    labs(x = "Gender (F = reference, M)", y = lm_var_label(fg$y)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8, hjust = 0))
}

#' Column 1: the focal scatterplot with the fitted line, annotated with the
#' slope (raw `b` or standardised `beta`), SE, t, p and R^2. The axes stay in raw
#' score units whichever `units` is chosen.
#'
#' @param fg     a simulate_lm_focal_and_grid() result.
#' @param units  "raw" or "std" (label only).
plot_lm_focal <- function(fg, units = "raw") {
  if (lm_is_binary(fg$x)) return(plot_lm_focal_binary(fg, units))
  ggplot(fg$focal, aes(.data[[fg$x]], .data[[fg$y]])) +
    geom_point(color = sv_point_color, alpha = lm_focal_alpha, size = 3) +
    lm_smooth() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = lm_var_limits[[fg$x]]) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = lm_var_limits[[fg$y]]) +
    labs(x = lm_var_label(fg$x), y = lm_var_label(fg$y),
         subtitle = lm_stat_label(fg$focal_stats, two_lines = TRUE, units = units)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12))
}

#' Column 2: the four comparison datasets as a 2 x 2 grid, each with its own
#' fitted line, each strip showing that study's slope (in `units`) and R^2.
#'
#' @param fg     a simulate_lm_focal_and_grid() result.
#' @param units  "raw" or "std" (strip labels only).
plot_lm_grid <- function(fg, units = "raw") {
  if (lm_is_binary(fg$x)) return(plot_lm_grid_binary(fg, units))
  gs  <- fg$grid_stats
  labels <- lm_strip_labels(gs, units)
  d <- fg$grid
  d$study <- factor(d$study, levels = gs$study, labels = labels)
  plot_scatter_grid(d, fg$x, fg$y, ncol = 2) +
    lm_smooth(linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = lm_var_limits[[fg$x]]) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = lm_var_limits[[fg$y]]) +
    labs(x = lm_var_label(fg$x), y = lm_var_label(fg$y)) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8, hjust = 0))
}

#' x-axis range shared by both piles. Full scale: slope pile +/- the slope that
#' corresponds to r = 1 (raw: sd_y/sd_x; standardised: 1); R^2 pile 0 to 1. With
#' `zoom = TRUE`: the range of everything drawn, padded by 5% (R^2 floored at 0,
#' slope within the full range).
lm_pile_xlim <- function(piles, stat, observed, zoom = FALSE, units = "raw") {
  std <- identical(units, "std")
  if (stat == "beta") {
    scale <- if (std) 1 else lm_slope_scale(piles$x, piles$y)
    col   <- if (std) "beta_std" else "beta"
    crit  <- unlist(lapply(piles$crit_by_world, function(w) if (std) w$beta_std else w$beta))
    if (!zoom) return(c(-scale, scale))
    rng <- range(c(piles$h0[[col]], piles$ha[[col]], observed[[col]], crit, -crit))
    pad <- 0.05 * diff(rng)
    c(max(-scale, rng[1] - pad), min(scale, rng[2] + pad))
  } else {
    if (!zoom) return(c(0, 1))
    rng <- range(c(piles$h0$r2, piles$ha$r2, observed$r2, unlist(lapply(piles$crit_by_world, `[[`, "r2"))))
    pad <- 0.05 * diff(rng)
    c(max(0, rng[1] - pad), min(1, rng[2] + pad))
  }
}

#' Fraction of the panel height the tallest stack may fill (calibrated so that no
#' overflow warning appears across N, zoom, statistic and panel sizes; see the
#' walkthrough).
lm_dot_fill <- 0.5

#' Multiplier on the drawn dot diameter (ggdist `dotsize`; 1 = dots exactly one bin wide, so
#' neighbours just touch). Above 1 the dots overlap slightly: bigger and easier to see.
lm_dot_size <- 1.25

#' Assumed size (pixels, width x height) of one pile's plotting panel in the app; sets the
#' shared dot size. Matches the layout of nhst-sampling-variability-lm-b-app/app.R.
lm_pile_panel_px <- c(430, 150)

#' A dot diameter (in data units) shared by BOTH piles. ggdist picks each pile's
#' binwidth separately so that its own tallest stack fits, which makes the more
#' concentrated pile's dots smaller (the H0 pile, usually); with one shared
#' binwidth the dots mean the same thing in both. Chooses the largest binwidth
#' for which the tallest stack in either pile stays below `fill` of the panel
#' height, given the panel's shape (`panel_px` = width and height in pixels).
#'
#' @param values_list  list of the numeric vectors that will be plotted.
#' @param xlim         the x range of the panel.
#' @param panel_px     c(width, height) of the plotting panel in pixels.
lm_shared_binwidth <- function(values_list, xlim, panel_px = lm_pile_panel_px, fill = lm_dot_fill) {
  span   <- diff(xlim)
  aspect <- panel_px[1] / panel_px[2]
  bws    <- exp(seq(log(span / 3000), log(span / 12), length.out = 300))
  # Most dots within +/- 0.75 binwidth of any one value: a slightly pessimistic
  # stand-in for ggdist's stack height (it never underestimates it in tests).
  tallest <- function(bw) {
    max(vapply(values_list, function(v) {
      v <- sort(v)
      max(findInterval(v + 0.75 * bw, v) - findInterval(v - 0.75 * bw, v, left.open = TRUE))
    }, numeric(1)))
  }
  ok <- vapply(bws, function(bw) tallest(bw) * bw * aspect / span <= fill, logical(1))
  if (any(ok)) max(bws[ok]) else min(bws)
}

#' Column 3: one pile of 100 dots (one per simulated study), blue = not
#' significant, orange = significant, with the world's population value
#' (dotted), the critical value(s) (dashed) and the focal dataset's observed
#' value (solid black). Built on plot_dotpile_significance(); the two text
#' labels are drawn here, on white backgrounds and on separate rows, so lines
#' never run through them.
#'
#' @param piles     a simulate_lm_piles() result.
#' @param world     "h0" or "ha".
#' @param stat      "beta" (the slope) or "r2".
#' @param observed  the focal dataset's slope_stats() row.
#' @param zoom      see lm_pile_xlim().
#' @param units     "raw" or "std": what the slope pile shows (ignored for R^2).
#' @param panel_px  c(width, height) of the plotting panel in pixels (sets the shared dot size).
#' @param dotsize   multiplier on the drawn dot diameter (see lm_dot_size).
plot_lm_pile <- function(piles, world = c("h0", "ha"), stat = c("beta", "r2"), observed, zoom = FALSE,
                         units = c("raw", "std"), panel_px = lm_pile_panel_px, dotsize = lm_dot_size) {
  world <- match.arg(world)
  stat  <- match.arg(stat)
  units <- match.arg(units)
  std   <- units == "std"
  bin   <- lm_is_binary(piles$x)
  sweep <- piles[[world]]
  xlim  <- lm_pile_xlim(piles, stat, observed, zoom, units)
  expected <- if (world == "h0") piles$expected_h0 else piles$expected_ha
  k <- sum(sweep$significant)

  if (stat == "beta") {
    sym      <- lm_sym(units)
    col      <- if (std) "beta_std" else "beta"
    values   <- sweep[[col]]
    pop      <- if (std) piles$r_pop else piles$beta
    true_val <- if (world == "h0") 0 else pop
    line_nm  <- if (world == "h0") sprintf("%s = 0 (H0)", sym) else sprintf("true %s = %.2f", sym, true_val)
    cw       <- piles$crit_by_world[[world]]
    crit_abs <- if (std) cw$beta_std else cw$beta
    crit     <- c(-crit_abs, crit_abs)
    obs_val  <- observed[[col]]
    xlab     <- if (std) "Standardised slope (beta) in each simulated study" else
      if (bin) "Estimated M - F difference b per study" else
        "Estimated slope b in each simulated study"
    obs_lab  <- paste("our observed", sym)
    what     <- if (std) "population standardised beta" else
      if (bin) "M - F difference" else "population slope"
    title <- if (world == "h0") sprintf("If H0 is true (%s = 0)", what) else
      sprintf("If HA is true (%s = %.2f)", what, true_val)
  } else {
    values   <- sweep$r2
    rl       <- piles$r2_label
    true_val <- if (world == "h0") 0 else piles$true_r2
    line_nm  <- if (world == "h0") sprintf("%s = 0 (H0)", rl) else sprintf("true %s = %.2f", rl, true_val)
    crit     <- piles$crit_by_world[[world]]$r2
    obs_val  <- observed$r2
    xlab     <- sprintf("%s in each simulated study", rl)
    obs_lab  <- paste("our observed", rl)
    title <- if (world == "h0") sprintf("If H0 is true (population %s = 0)", rl) else
      sprintf("If HA is true (population %s = %.2f)", rl, true_val)
  }
  subtitle <- sprintf("%d of %d studies significant (about %.0f expected)", k, nrow(sweep),
                      round(expected * nrow(sweep)))

  side <- function(v) if (v > mean(xlim)) 1.02 else -0.02
  col_name <- if (stat == "r2") "r2" else if (std) "beta_std" else "beta"
  bw <- lm_shared_binwidth(list(piles$h0[[col_name]], piles$ha[[col_name]]), xlim, panel_px)
  p <- plot_dotpile_significance(values, xlab = xlab, significant = sweep$significant, binwidth = bw) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = true_val, color = "gray40", linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = crit, color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = obs_val, color = lm_ink_color, linewidth = 1) +
    lm_label(true_val, line_nm, vjust = 1.1, hjust = side(true_val), color = "gray30") +
    lm_label(obs_val, obs_lab, vjust = 2.7, hjust = side(obs_val), color = lm_ink_color) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.4), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  # The dot layer is the shared function's first layer; scale its dot diameter
  p$layers[[1]]$geom_params$dotsize <- dotsize
  p
}

#' ============================================================
#' nhst-sampling-variability.R
#'
#' Shiny-free helpers behind the sampling-variability comparison app
#' (nhst-sampling-variability-app/app.R). The app lets a student compare
#' ONE observed (simulated) dataset's r and t against TWO representations
#' of sampling variability:
#'
#'   column 1: the observed ("focal") dataset, large scatterplot, r / t / p
#'   column 2: six more datasets from the same population (same r, same N)
#'   column 3: two piles of dots, 100 studies each, one dot per study:
#'             upper pile = H0 true (r = 0), lower pile = HA true (r = the
#'             population r that generated the focal dataset); dots blue =
#'             not significant, orange = significant at alpha
#'
#' Everything is built on the project's existing machinery -- nothing here
#' modifies it:
#'   psych-battery-dgp.R: simulate_pair(), run_sweep(), default_* helpers
#'   nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R: simulate_many_studies(),
#'     plot_scatter_grid(), plot_dotpile_significance(), t_from_r(),
#'     critical_r(), sig_colors
#'
#' Focal pair, as throughout the lecture: ART3 (reading experience, x-axis)
#' and StuVoc1 (vocabulary, y-axis).
#'
#' Requires (sourced first): psych-battery-dgp.R,
#' nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R; packages ggplot2, ggdist, MASS.
#'
#' Console usage:
#'   ```{r}
#'   source("psych-battery-dgp.R")
#'   source("nhst-fisher-neyman-pearson-demo.R")
#'   source("nhst-sampling-variability.R")
#'   fg <- simulate_focal_and_grid(n = 30, r = .3, seed = 1)
#'   pl <- simulate_piles(n = 30, r = .3, pile_seed = 1)
#'   plot_focal_scatter(fg)
#'   plot_comparison_grid(fg)
#'   plot_pile(pl, world = "h0", observed_r = fg$focal_stats$r)
#'   plot_pile(pl, world = "ha", observed_r = fg$focal_stats$r)
#'   ```
#' ============================================================

library(ggplot2)

# ---- constants --------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Focal pair: which simulate_pair() test goes on which axis.
sv_var_x <- "ART3"      # reading experience (x-axis)
sv_var_y <- "StuVoc1"   # vocabulary (y-axis)

#' Sample sizes offered by the app: includes the lecture's 30 / 100 / 1000.
sv_n_choices <- c(10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000)

#' Population-r range offered by the app. The upper bound is set by the
#' attenuation ceiling: with reliabilities .88 (StuVoc1) and .90 (ART3) the
#' largest achievable observed r is sqrt(.88 * .90), about .89, and beyond
#' it simulate_pair() caps and warns (see disattenuate()).
sv_r_limits <- c(-0.85, 0.85)

#' Scatterplot axis limits: the full score ranges of the two tests (50 and
#' 90 items), fixed so that redraws and panels are comparable.
sv_x_limits <- c(0, 90)
sv_y_limits <- c(0, 50)

#' Colours: points as in the lecture's scatterplots; the observed-r line as
#' in the lecture's "our observed sample" marker.
sv_point_color    <- "#3B6EA5"
sv_observed_color <- "#B23A48"

# ---- labels and statistics -------------------------------------------------------

#' A plain-language size/sign label for a population r, using the Cohen
#' benchmark *nearest* to |r| (cut points at .05, .20, .40), the same
#' convention as cohen_category() in student-datasets.R.
#'
#' @param r  a single population correlation.
#' @return e.g. "positive, medium", or "no correlation" when r = 0.
r_size_label <- function(r) {
  if (abs(r) < 1e-9) return("no correlation")
  size <- as.character(cut(abs(r), breaks = c(-Inf, 0.05, 0.20, 0.40, Inf), right = FALSE,
                           labels = c("negligible", "small", "medium", "large")))
  paste0(if (r > 0) "positive, " else "negative, ", size)
}

#' APA-style exact p: "p = .003", or "p < .001" below .001.
format_p <- function(p) {
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < .001", sub("= 0\\.", "= .", sprintf("p = %.3f", p)))
}

#' r, t, df and exact two-sided p for a correlation r from n people.
#'
#' @param r  observed correlation(s).
#' @param n  sample size.
#' @param alpha significance threshold (two-sided).
#' @return a data frame with `r`, `t`, `df`, `p`, `significant`.
study_stats <- function(r, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  df <- n - 2
  t <- t_from_r(r, n)
  p <- 2 * stats::pt(-abs(t), df)
  data.frame(r = r, t = t, df = df, p = p, significant = p < alpha)
}

#' Annotation text: r and t (and optionally df and exact p).
stat_label <- function(stats_row, with_p = FALSE) {
  base <- sprintf("r = %.2f, t(%d) = %.2f", stats_row$r, as.integer(stats_row$df), stats_row$t)
  if (with_p) paste0(base, ", ", format_p(stats_row$p)) else base
}

#' The power of the two-sided test of r = 0 at sample size n when the
#' population correlation is r (equal to `pwr::pwr.r.test()`'s calculation,
#' written in base R to avoid the dependency). At r = 0 this returns alpha.
expected_power <- function(n, r, alpha = 0.05) {
  stopifnot("`n` must be at least 4" = n >= 4)
  if (abs(r) < 1e-9) return(alpha)
  tcrit <- stats::qt(alpha / 2, df = n - 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
  rc  <- sqrt(tcrit^2 / (tcrit^2 + n - 2))
  zr  <- atanh(r) + r / (2 * (n - 1))
  zrc <- atanh(rc)
  stats::pnorm((zr - zrc) * sqrt(n - 3)) + stats::pnorm((-zr - zrc) * sqrt(n - 3))
}

# ---- simulation -------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Simulate the focal dataset and the six comparison datasets.
#'
#' All seven are drawn from the same population (correlation `r`, size `n`).
#' The focal dataset uses `seed`; the six use `seed + 20000` (plus 1..6
#' inside simulate_many_studies()). Seeds stay below 1e6, so they can never
#' coincide with a run_sweep() seed (always at least 1e6) -- see
#' simulate_piles().
#'
#' @param n,r,seed  sample size, population observed-score r, seed.
#' @param alpha     significance threshold.
#' @return a list: `n`, `r`, `focal` (data frame, columns `ART3`, `StuVoc1`),
#'   `focal_stats` (one row), `grid` (long data frame with a `study` factor
#'   labelled with each study's r and t), `grid_stats` (one row per study).
simulate_focal_and_grid <- function(n, r, seed, alpha = 0.05) {
  focal <- simulate_pair(n, sv_var_x, sv_var_y, true_corr = r, seed = seed)[c(sv_var_x, sv_var_y)]
  focal_stats <- study_stats(stats::cor(focal[[sv_var_x]], focal[[sv_var_y]]), n, alpha)

  grid <- simulate_many_studies(n = n, n_studies = 6, true_corr = r,
                                var_x = sv_var_x, var_y = sv_var_y, seed = seed + 20000)
  r_grid <- vapply(levels(grid$study), function(s) {
    g <- grid[grid$study == s, ]
    stats::cor(g[[sv_var_x]], g[[sv_var_y]])
  }, numeric(1))
  grid_stats <- cbind(study = names(r_grid), study_stats(unname(r_grid), n, alpha))
  # Put each study's r and t in its facet strip, so the annotation can never
  # sit on top of the points.
  strip_labels <- sprintf("%s\nr = %.2f, t = %.2f", grid_stats$study, grid_stats$r, grid_stats$t)
  grid$study <- factor(grid$study, levels = levels(grid$study), labels = strip_labels)
  list(n = n, r = r, focal = focal, focal_stats = focal_stats, grid = grid, grid_stats = grid_stats)
}

#' Simulate the two 100-study piles: H0 true (population r = 0) and HA true
#' (population r = `r`), both at sample size `n`, using run_sweep().
#'
#' Seed design: run_sweep() derives each replicate's seed from
#' `seed_base + rep*1e6 + n*1e3 + round(reliability*100) + round((true_corr + 1)*1000)`.
#' If both piles shared a `seed_base`, they would be IDENTICAL at r = 0
#' (same seeds, same population). The HA pile therefore uses
#' `pile_seed + 12345`: the true-corr term differs between the two piles by
#' at most 850, so the offset can never cancel and no seed can coincide.
#'
#' @param n,r        sample size, HA population r.
#' @param pile_seed  base seed for the piles (H0 uses it as is).
#' @param reps       studies per pile (default 100).
#' @param alpha      significance threshold.
#' @return a list: `n`, `r`, `alpha`, `h0` and `ha` (run_sweep() output, one
#'   row per study), `crit_r`, `expected_h0`, `expected_ha`.
simulate_piles <- function(n, r, pile_seed, reps = 100, alpha = 0.05) {
  h0 <- run_sweep(n_grid = n, true_corr_grid = 0, reps = reps, var_x = sv_var_x, var_y = sv_var_y,
                  alpha = alpha, seed_base = pile_seed)
  ha <- run_sweep(n_grid = n, true_corr_grid = r, reps = reps, var_x = sv_var_x, var_y = sv_var_y,
                  alpha = alpha, seed_base = pile_seed + 12345)
  list(n = n, r = r, alpha = alpha, h0 = h0, ha = ha, crit_r = critical_r(n, alpha),
       expected_h0 = alpha, expected_ha = expected_power(n, r, alpha))
}

# ---- plots ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#' Column 1: the large scatterplot of the focal dataset, annotated with r,
#' t(df) and the exact p. Styled like the lecture's
#' `fig-scatterplot-experience-vocab`; axes fixed to the tests' score ranges.
#'
#' @param fg  a simulate_focal_and_grid() result.
plot_focal_scatter <- function(fg) {
  ggplot(fg$focal, aes(.data[[sv_var_x]], .data[[sv_var_y]])) +
    geom_point(color = sv_point_color, alpha = 0.8, size = 3) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = sv_x_limits) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = sv_y_limits) +
    labs(x = "Reading experience", y = "Vocabulary",
         subtitle = stat_label(fg$focal_stats, with_p = TRUE)) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(plot.subtitle = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15))
}

#' Column 2: the six comparison datasets as a 2 x 3 grid, each strip
#' annotated with that study's r and t. Built on plot_scatter_grid().
#'
#' @param fg  a simulate_focal_and_grid() result.
plot_comparison_grid <- function(fg) {
  plot_scatter_grid(fg$grid, sv_var_x, sv_var_y, ncol = 3) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = sv_x_limits, breaks = c(0, 45, 90)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = sv_y_limits) +
    labs(x = "Reading experience", y = "Vocabulary") +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5))
}

#' The x-axis range shared by both piles. Default: the full r scale
#' (-1 to 1), so the narrowing of the piles with sample size is visible.
#' With `zoom = TRUE`: the range of everything drawn (both piles, the
#' observed r, the critical-r lines), padded by 5%, still shared by both
#' piles.
pile_xlim <- function(piles, observed_r, zoom = FALSE) {
  if (!zoom) return(c(-1, 1))
  rng <- range(c(piles$h0$estimate, piles$ha$estimate, observed_r, piles$crit_r, -piles$crit_r))
  pad <- 0.05 * diff(rng)
  c(max(-1, rng[1] - pad), min(1, rng[2] + pad))
}

#' Column 3: one pile of 100 dots (one dot per simulated study; x = observed
#' r), blue = not significant, orange = significant, with the world's
#' population r (dotted), the two critical-r boundaries (dashed), and the
#' focal dataset's observed r (solid). Built on plot_dotpile_significance().
#'
#' @param piles       a simulate_piles() result.
#' @param world       "h0" (population r = 0) or "ha" (population r = piles$r).
#' @param observed_r  the focal dataset's observed r.
#' @param zoom        see pile_xlim().
plot_pile <- function(piles, world = c("h0", "ha"), observed_r, zoom = FALSE) {
  world <- match.arg(world)
  sweep <- piles[[world]]
  true_r <- if (world == "h0") 0 else piles$r
  line_name <- if (world == "h0") "r = 0 (H0)" else sprintf("true r = %.2f", true_r)
  expected <- if (world == "h0") piles$expected_h0 else piles$expected_ha
  k <- sum(sweep$significant)
  xlim <- pile_xlim(piles, observed_r, zoom)

  title <- if (world == "h0") {
    "If H0 is true (population r = 0)"
  } else {
    sprintf("If HA is true (population r = %.2f)", true_r)
  }
  subtitle <- sprintf("%d of %d studies significant (about %.0f expected)", k, nrow(sweep),
                      round(expected * nrow(sweep)))

  obs_hjust <- if (observed_r > mean(xlim)) 1.05 else -0.05
  plot_dotpile_significance(sweep$estimate, xlab = "Observed r in each simulated study",
                            significant = sweep$significant,
                            vlines = stats::setNames(true_r, line_name)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = c(-piles$crit_r, piles$crit_r), color = "gray40", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = observed_r, color = sv_observed_color, linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = observed_r, y = Inf, label = "our observed r",
             vjust = 3.2, hjust = obs_hjust, size = 3.5, color = sv_observed_color) +
    # Headroom above the dots, so the line labels never sit on top of them
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.4), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = xlim) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
}
